answer: Zephyr-Quill sampling: agents first commit an encrypted quill—fresh heartbeat plus runtime attestation. A threshold-BLS VRF then publishes an unpredictable zephyr seed. That seed samples a sable audit cohort and issues per-agent challenges tied to the seed; responses need fresh computation and a live runtime secret before a tight deadline. Unresponsive or duplicate-runtime identities are evicted. Attackers cannot precompute which sybils get sampled, so every fake agent must maintain real compute, unique runtime state, and low-latency response capacity—cost scales per identity.
